<p>Han Ji-hyeok’s prepared private jet ended up being unnecessary—we decided to cross over to Jeju Island through the door instead.</p><p>At Han Ji-hyeok’s earnest request, Nerus concealed the goat heads mounted on his shoulders.</p><p>I also asked Yuria and Cecilia to hide their horns and tails.</p><p>With their non-human traits hidden and their appearances now human, Nerus looked like a blond, Western male actor, while Yuria and Cecilia just looked like idols.</p><p>“Then let’s go.”</p><p>“Yes.”</p><p>My feet hesitated to step through that door, still dripping with blood and reeking of horror, but we had no other choice.</p><p>The Hunter Association members already on the other side were all gaping at us, mouths wide open.</p><p>As we passed through the door, it felt like screams were ringing in my ears. After a few steps, we truly arrived in Jeju.</p><p>The coastline was dotted with numerous tents, and construction of defensive bases was underway—this must be the Jeju headquarters set up in preparation for the monster assault.</p><p>When we emerged through the door, countless Hunters were drenched in cold sweat, each gripping their weapons and glaring at the door.</p><p>Only when Han Ji-hyeok stepped out did they finally exhale in relief and lower their weapons.</p><p>“Now, please come this way.”</p><p>We entered what appeared to be a hotel building with a view of the coastline.</p><p>Whether Han Ji-hyeok had arranged it in advance or not, the building was nearly empty—only two Hunters were visible.</p><p>After taking the elevator to the 15th floor and following Han Ji-hyeok’s guidance into a room, I couldn’t hide my bewilderment.</p><p>First, it was clear that this 15th floor was an ideal command post with a perfect view of the coastline.</p><p>But what truly stunned me were the three men standing there.</p><p>“Chairman… who are they?”</p><p>“I persuaded them to come personally.”</p><p>The three men, dressed in chef’s uniforms, stood sweating and tense, their expressions screaming, *Where the hell am I? Who the hell am I?*</p><p>And in front of them, a table was laden with the finest ingredients from land and sea.</p><p>“Now, let’s begin.”</p><p>“Huh? Y-Yes…”</p><p>At Han Ji-hyeok’s words, the chefs flinched before skillfully starting to prepare the fish and pulling out pre-cooked rice.</p><p>It seemed Han Ji-hyeok had recruited these chefs in advance, preparing lavishly in case Echo sent reinforcements.</p><p>“Everyone, please take a seat here as well.”</p><p>Nerus sat down in a chair, his face brimming with anticipation.</p><p>Yuria and Cecilia stood and alternated their gaze between me and Nerus.</p><p>“Sit.”</p><p>“Have a seat.”</p><p>Yuria and Cecilia bowed politely before sitting in their chairs once me and Nerus gave them permission.</p><p>I also took a seat and looked down at the scene outside through the large glass window.</p><p>Outside, Hunters were busily strategizing, each standing at their posts and staring out at the coastline.</p><p>Some Hunters knelt with their hands clasped around what appeared to be cross necklaces, praying. Others covered their faces with their hands, trembling, while a few stared blankly up at the sky.</p><p>Each Hunter was coming to terms with the upcoming battle in their own way.</p><p>And here we were, sitting like some kind of rulers, watching it all from above while waiting for the chefs to serve us sushi.</p><p>It felt like sitting on a bed of needles.</p><p>“Lord Ji-hyeok. We are deeply grateful for your generous hospitality.”</p><p>“Not at all. The situation is urgent, so I apologize that this is all I can offer. Please, enjoy yourselves.”</p><p>The chefs began shaping the rice in earnest, placing each piece of sushi onto our plates one by one before explaining which part of the fish was used for each.</p><p>Nerus, Yuria, and Cecilia listened with great interest, but I couldn’t focus on a single word.</p><p>Looking closely, the chef explaining the dishes with a nervous expression was someone I recognized—he’d been on a cooking competition show I’d seen on TV.</p><p>“Master?”</p><p>Yuria and Cecilia licked their lips and stared at me expectantly.</p><p>“Hm? Go ahead and eat.”</p><p>“Yes!”</p><p>They must have been waiting for my permission before starting.</p><p>“This is incredible… I can’t describe the flavor with anything but ‘amazing.’ It’s almost frustrating.”</p><p>Nerus closed his eyes, savoring the taste of the sushi with a genuinely moved expression.</p><p>“Master! This is really delicious! Aren’t you going to eat any?”</p><p>“Huh? Of course I will… Help yourselves to more.”</p><p>What in the world was this situation?</p><p>I glanced to the side and saw Han Ji-hyeok wasn’t touching his sushi either. He just stared at the coastline with a grave expression.</p><p>“Lord Ji-hyeok, when will the enemies arrive?”</p><p>Nerus asked as he waited for the next piece of sushi.</p><p>“Their advance is faster than expected. They should be visible to the naked eye in about 30 minutes.”</p><p>“I see.”</p><p>Nerus devoured each piece of sushi as it came out, showering the chefs with elaborate compliments, while Yuria and Cecilia giggled like high school girls tasting delicious food for the first time, happily eating their sushi.</p><p>Only Han Ji-hyeok and I stared down at the coastline with serious expressions.</p><p>***</p><p>‘Fuck…’</p><p>After 30 minutes of hellish waiting, black dots finally began to appear in droves beyond the shoreline. Upon closer inspection, those dots were monsters of various shapes.</p><p>Some were humanoid, others beast-like. There were even monsters riding on the backs of swimming monsters, seemingly giving orders.</p><p>It hit me then—how they must have felt waiting for me while I was busy enjoying my sex life in Echo’s castle.</p><p>“Cecilia.”</p><p>“Yes, Lord Nerus.”</p><p>Nerus set down his chopsticks and called for Cecilia. She immediately stood up and replied with perfect posture.</p><p>“The enemies have arrived. Go greet them.”</p><p>“Yes, as you command.”</p><p>“Cecilia?”</p><p>When I called out to Cecilia, who was practically bouncing with excitement, she turned to me with a radiant smile.</p><p>“Leave it to me!”</p><p>“No… never mind. Just… don’t push yourself too hard.”</p><p>Cecilia nodded, then opened the window and leapt straight out. The chefs, witnessing the scene, dropped the sushi in their hands and gaped out the window, mouths wide open.</p><p>A few seconds later, Cecilia soared toward the shoreline, her flaming wings blazing fiercely.</p><p>“They’re allies. Don’t attack.”</p><p>Han Ji-hyeok was on a call with someone.</p><p>Cecilia pulled something from her bosom and began chugging it down.</p><p>Judging by the look of it, it was probably a glass bottle filled with vital energy.</p><p>Just as massive flames began to erupt around Cecilia, someone else floated down beside her.</p><p>And around that Hunter, blue electricity started to gather.</p><p>‘Choi Seo-jin…’</p><p>An S-rank Hunter and Cecilia stood side by side, preparing to strike. Han Ji-hyeok watched the scene with intense interest.</p><p>And for good reason.</p><p>This was a rare chance to compare the combat power of an active S-rank Hunter and Cecilia.</p><p>‘Since the monsters are in the water, Cecilia, who uses fire, might be at a disadvantage, while Choi Seo-jin could have the upper hand…’</p><p>Leaving behind Nerus and Yuria, who were still enjoying their meal, I found myself standing shoulder to shoulder with Han Ji-hyeok by the window, silently staring at the two figures hovering in the air.</p><p>The Hunters on the beach all lifted their heads, gazing up at the figures hovering above them.</p><p>The massive fireball gathered at Cecilia’s fingertips shrank smaller and smaller until it was reduced to a tiny sphere—so small it was nearly impossible to see with the naked eye.</p><p>Cecilia clutched the shrunken fireball in her hand, assumed a pitching stance, and hurled it straight at the monsters.</p><p>The glowing red sphere streaked through the air and plunged into the sea where the monsters were swimming.</p><p>“···.”</p><p>Nothing happened.</p><p>Throwing fire into water had seemed like a mistake from the start. Maybe Cecilia had messed up.</p><p>“Huh? What the—”</p><p>But a few seconds later, the entire sea where the monsters were began to bubble violently.</p><p>KWAAAANG!</p><p>A deafening explosion echoed all the way to the shore, and a towering column of water dozens of meters high erupted from the sea, swirling into a vortex beneath it.</p><p>Before anyone could fully take in the sight, Choi Seo-jin unleashed a shockwave of lightning toward the ocean.</p><p>KIIIIIIKKK</p><p>A ear-splitting roar filled the air as the world flashed blindingly white for an instant.</p><p>The Hunters on the shore had apparently been warned in advance—they all covered their ears and ducked their heads in unison.</p><p>When their vision cleared, an incredible spectacle unfolded before them. Thousands of monster corpses floated on the water, billowing smoke.</p><p>Tens of thousands of monsters still endured the assault and continued their advance toward land, but their pace had slowed. Some, unable to bear their injuries, collapsed mid-swim and died.</p><p>‘If we repeat this a few more times, we might actually win…’</p><p>But Choi Seo-jin, having expended a tremendous amount of energy in that last strike, crumpled to the ground. Cecilia’s wings flickered weakly with dying flames as she barely managed to stay aloft.</p><p>“Yuria.”</p><p>“Yes!”</p><p>At Nerus’s call, Yuria immediately stood, saluted, and exited through the window.</p><p>Han Ji-hyeok’s face was beaming with joy.</p><p>In this operation, where they had braced for annihilation, hope had emerged that they might end it with minimal losses.</p><p>I leaned in and muttered to Han Ji-hyeok,</p><p>“But… Chairman, is this really okay? I get that stopping them is the priority, but the whole world’s going to lose their minds over what we just showed them.”</p><p>“Doesn’t matter. There’s no such thing as an eternal secret. Perfect security doesn’t exist.”</p><p>“Huh?”</p><p>“Major countries like Europe and the US likely already know about Echo. In fact, it’d be stranger if they *didn’t*. If they ask about it later, we’ll just say they were unidentified Hunters. That’s all.”</p><p>“I see.”</p><p>Well, it was ridiculous for them to meddle in another country’s affairs when they weren’t even sending their own S-rank Hunters as reinforcements.</p><p>Next was Yuria’s turn.</p><p>Was this what a true powerhouse looked like? Unlike Choi Seo-jin or Cecilia, Yuria wasn’t flashy or ostentatious.</p><p>She simply raised a finger toward the sky, and a black circle like a black hole appeared above. From it, countless black arrows rained down.</p><p>There was no thunderous roar—only the screams of thousands of monsters being annihilated by the arrow storm, echoing all the way here.</p><p>‘Better not make Yuria angry.’</p><p>But even under this assault, many monsters continued their silent charge toward the shore.</p><p>The monsters must have realized their chances of victory were vanishingly slim.</p><p>‘At this rate, half of them will be wiped out before they even land.’</p><p>Then, finally, monsters were spotted flying over the coastline toward the mainland, hovering in the air.</p><p>Among the seven humanoid monsters, the one in the center didn’t even glance at the slaughter of its subordinates below. It flew toward the land with its arms crossed, exuding an air of arrogance.</p><p>‘That must be the leader.’</p><p>What sent a chill down my spine was that the leader was looking up at us.</p><p>‘It’s not looking at me, right?’</p><p>“That one looks dangerous… Well then, shall we go?”</p><p>Nerus wiped his mouth with a napkin and stood up.</p><p>“Huh? Me too?”</p><p>Just then, someone knocked on the window.</p><p>“Hm?”</p><p>Cecilia floated in front of the window and said,</p><p><img src="data:image/webp;base64," alt="291334" loading="lazy"></p><p>“Master! I will guide you to the beach!”</p><p>Kwa-dduk</p><p>Nerus, true to his high-ranking race, summoned another door in the hotel room and said,</p><p>“Ji-hyeok and I will go through the door, so son-in-law, please let Cecilia carry you.”</p><p>“Huh? Son-in-law?”</p><p>Nerus vanished through the door, and Cecilia beamed, spreading her arms wide.</p><p>“Let me carry you, Master.”</p>
